doc.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019

title: Chitlin Circuit repertoire and playing at Porky's
summary: Rhythm and blues meant rhythm changes and blues; Longo subbed for Cannonball's pianist at Porky's club run by Porky Pineko.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: What kind of tunes would you have played on the Chitlin Circuit?

Oh see, back then, this was before rock & roll. And so, I don’t know if you remember Earl Bostic, you remember him? The kind of stuff he was playing is what was popular because Elvis and all that stuff hadn’t started yet. So we’d be playing “Night Train” and if you knew the blues, down there, in Florida, I don’t know man whether anybody — but the term “rhythm & blues” meant the changes to “I Got Rhythm” and blues changes. So when you played a rhythm & blues gig, if you could play “I Got Rhythm” changes and blues changes in C, G, F, B flat, and if you were really hip you could play “One O’clock Jump” in D flat. And so that’s what those gigs were you know. So the one I remember mostly was “Night Train.” That was very popular back then. And a lot of them didn’t have names man. Cannonball wrote a lot of tunes, they later on became on his first

album. Because I played with him at this club called Porky’s in Fort Lauderdale. You know those Porky movies? That was a real place. That was Fort Lauderdale and in the movie it was Angel Beach. And they had Porky as this redneck guy with a cowboy hat. No, man, Porky was a gangster. He was Porky Pineko. And he loved jazz. And he booked Cannonball’s group and I was just a kid in high school and Cannonball’s piano player got busted for something. So he calls my mother, middle of the night, and says, “Mrs. Longo, you think you could let young Michael come down to finish the week with us?” So she let me go down and I finished the week at Porky’s with him. That’s how that all started.
